title: Biomass Digestion and ICP-OES Operation Protocol
author: Maria F. Duran
materials: Safety Data Sheet for nitric acid

Chemicals 70% Nitric acid (HNO3) Supplies Biomass (agricultural waste, ash) 50 mL conical Falcon tubes 15 mL conical Falcon tubes 2ml glass pipettes Centrifuge filter tubes 0.45um Equipment Chemical fume hood Bench-top centrifuge (capable of accommodating 5ml Falcon tubes) Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometer (ICP-OES)

Instrument Setup Open the ICP Expert software and confirm the instrument is connected Verify purges are complete Install, rinse, and outlet tubing correctly Start rinsing the autosampler and instrument Turn on the chiller, wait for -38 °C , then ignite the plasma Let the plasma stabilize for about 00:15:00

Method Setup In the software: Open an existing worksheet/template or create a new quantitative worksheet Select elements and wavelengths Assign axial or radial viewing conditions Define calibration standards and blanks Set QC options such as the continuing calibration blank ( CCB), the continuing calibration verification ( CCV), and the initial calibration verification ( ICV).

Run Setup and Analysis Arrange standards, QC solutions, and samples in the autosampler racks Example S Rack configuration for ICP analysis. The center autosampler rack (S Rack) includes fixed positions for key quality control solutions: blank (CCB) in S1:3 and standard (CCV) in S1:4. Staff-use positions are reserved and should not be disturbed. Assign rack and tube positions in the sequence Check that all samples to be analyzed are selected Start the run and confirm the first standards and samples run correctly Review spectra and confirm suitable analytical wavelengths during the run

steps.title: Prepare Fume Hood and Workstation
steps.instruction: Set up the workstation inside a functioning chemical fume hood (recommended flow rate 80-120 fpm, optimum face velocity ~100 fpm at 18-inch sash).

substeps.instruction: Place a pig mat inside the fume hood.
Position the sample rack on top of the pig mat.

steps.title: Prepare Biomass Ash Samples
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.10 g of biomass ash into individual 50 mL Falcon tubes.

substeps.instruction: Limit processing to no more than 10 samples per batch (e.g., 5 samples and 5 duplicates).

steps.title: Add Nitric Acid
steps.instruction: Add 70% nitric acid to the ash samples within the fume hood using glass pipettes to minimize dripping and vapor exposure.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 20 mL of 70% nitric acid into a 50 mL glass reservoir bottle.
Transfer 1 mL of 70% nitric acid from the reservoir into each ash sample tube using a 1–2 mL glass pipette.
Immediately place the cap loosely on each tube to minimize evaporation and fumes while preventing pressure buildup.

steps.title: Incubate Samples
steps.instruction: Digest the samples at room temperature in the fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Place the rack of capped sample tubes into a labeled secondary containment vessel.
Incubate for 48:00:00.

steps.title: Dilute Digest
steps.instruction: Dilute the digested samples to a final nitric acid concentration of 2% using deionized (DI) water.

substeps.instruction: Add 34 mL of DI water to each tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge Samples
steps.instruction: Filter the diluted samples using a bench-top centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Transfer approximately 10 mL of each sample into 0.45 µm centrifuge filter tubes and tighten caps.
Place filter tubes into centrifuge bucket racks inside the fume hood.
Securely close the buckets and transport them to the centrifuge.
Centrifuge at 4000 rpm and 22 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Collect Final Samples
steps.instruction: Collect 10 mL of the filtered supernatant into 15 mL Falcon tubes for ICP analysis.

steps.title: Handle and Dispose of Waste
steps.instruction: Process all waste containing 2% nitric acid using acid-compatible containers.

substeps.instruction: Filter waste through cheesecloth to separate liquid and solid fractions.

Collect liquid waste in a labeled, acid-compatible container; neutralize if acid concentration exceeds 5% by weight (~0.8 M or pH < 1) or if organic constituents are present before disposal via Waste Management Services.
Rinse solid material on cheesecloth with water, place in a sealed Ziploc bag, and discard in a biohazardous waste container.
Collect empty tubes, pipettes, and tips in an acid-compatible waste container for requisition.

steps.title: Perform Quality Assessment
steps.instruction: Assess ICP data quality using reliable wavelengths with sharp, symmetrical peaks and minimal interference.

substeps.instruction: Confirm peaks remain sharp and symmetrical at high standard concentrations; re-center spectral markers if needed.
Review unknown spectra, replicate consistency, and calibration curves.
Verify that the Percent RSD is ≤10%.

steps.title: Shutdown and Clean ICP
steps.instruction: Perform the ICP system shutdown and cleaning sequence.

substeps.instruction: Rinse the torch with rinse solution for 00:10:00 while plasma is on.
Turn off the plasma, then turn off the chiller.
Rinse the tubing system for 00:10:00.
Flush all lines dry with air.
Park the autosampler.
Release and unclip tubing as required.
Remove samples and dispose of waste properly.
